titleParts: Why Is India's GCC Hiring Boom Actually
intro: India's Global Capability Centre boom is straining on the supply of skilled talent as much as it is a branding challenge, because a large share of candidates cannot distinguish one GCC from another, and that recall gap is directly linked to higher attrition and slower hiring.
takeaways: Over 1,850 GCCs operate in India employing nearly 2 million professionals
45% of mid-level engineers cannot name 3 GCCs they would want to work for
Voluntary attrition averages 16-22%, spiking to 25-30% for senior AI/ML roles
Glassdoor and AmbitionBox ratings checked by nearly every candidate pre-offer
GCCs with strong branding see 20-30% lower 12-month attrition

body.text: How big is the India GCC hiring boom right now?

Large and still growing. Taggd's 2026 GCC hiring trends report cites more than 1,850 GCCs now operating in India, employing close to 2 million professionals, with volume hiring fading in favor of niche skills that command salary premiums reported as high as 1.7 times standard rates. Separately, Phoenix Talent's 2026 employer branding guide reports mid-market GCCs are projected to add roughly 40,000 jobs by the end of 2026, pushing total GCC headcount toward 260,000 in that segment alone, with total demand for experienced talent exceeding 500,000 positions across the sector in 2026. These figures come from recruiting and staffing industry sources, so treat the exact numbers as directional rather than independently audited.
What does the actual employer branding gap look like?

Concerning, according to multiple 2026 sources. Quantalent AI's GCC retention analysis reports that employer branding gaps leave 45% of mid-level engineers unable to name three GCCs they would want to work for, even as capability centers in Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune, and Chennai are reportedly losing senior engineers to startups at attrition rates above 22%. Omnivoo's 2026 GCC talent acquisition guide notes that mid and senior-level Indian engineers now receive 5 to 15 recruiter messages per week, meaning standing out requires deliberate, sustained employer branding rather than occasional job postings, since most candidates in a market this crowded have simply never heard of a given parent company's India operations.
Does attrition data actually support this being a branding problem, not just a pay problem?

The reported numbers suggest branding compounds a pay-driven baseline rather than being separate from it. Quantalent AI, citing Aon's 2025 India Salary Increase Survey, reports voluntary attrition averaging 16 to 22% across GCCs generally, spiking to 25 to 30% for AI/ML and senior engineering roles specifically, the exact segment facing the steepest talent competition. GCCs with pre-vetted, well-communicated hiring pipelines reportedly see 20 to 30% lower 12-month attrition compared to GCCs relying on generic agency pipelines, according to the same source, suggesting that hiring-quality and brand clarity compound each other rather than acting as separate levers.
What are candidates actually checking before they accept a GCC role?

Review platforms, consistently. Omnivoo states Glassdoor and AmbitionBox ratings are checked by nearly every candidate before accepting an interview, making active review management a practical, non-optional part of the hiring funnel rather than a reputational nicety. SansoviGCC's employer branding checklist for GCCs treats Glassdoor and AmbitionBox review monitoring, LinkedIn company page activity, and quarterly employer brand scorecards as baseline operational requirements for any GCC running an active hiring pipeline in India, not optional add-ons.
What should a GCC actually do about this in India specifically?

Invest in a specific, differentiated narrative rather than generic parent-company messaging, since the core problem multiple sources describe is candidates being unable to name or distinguish GCCs from each other. Actively manage Glassdoor and AmbitionBox presence with genuine employee reviews and response strategies, since these platforms are checked by nearly every candidate rather than a minority. Keep engineering leaders visible on LinkedIn with real technical content and team-culture posts, which Omnivoo describes as directly building organic reach among the exact senior engineers hardest to retain. And treat employer branding spend as retention infrastructure, not just a hiring-funnel cost, given the reported correlation between brand clarity, hiring quality, and lower 12-month attrition.
FAQ
How many GCCs are currently operating in India?
Industry sources report more than 1,850 GCCs operating in India as of 2026, employing close to 2 million professionals, with continued headcount growth projected through the year.
Is GCC attrition in India primarily a pay problem or a branding problem?

Both compound each other. Reported voluntary attrition runs 16 to 22% across GCCs generally and 25 to 30% for senior AI/ML roles specifically, and industry sources link employer branding gaps directly to higher attrition and slower, costlier hiring in this segment.
Do candidates actually check Glassdoor and AmbitionBox before accepting a GCC job in India?
Yes. Industry sources describe review-platform checks as close to universal among candidates evaluating a GCC offer, making active review management a practical hiring-funnel requirement.
What is the most common employer branding gap among Indian GCCs?

Industry data suggests a large share of mid-level engineers cannot name three GCCs they would want to work for, reflecting a lack of distinct, memorable employer branding relative to the number of GCCs actively competing for the same talent pool.
